title: How to fix AI written job descriptions on Mac for better hiring results
metaTitle: Fix AI written job descriptions: A guide for recruiters on Mac
description: Stop posting generic AI written job descriptions. Learn how to audit AI drafts, remove bias, and attract better candidates using your Mac.
intro: AI written job descriptions often fail to attract the right talent because they lack specific company context. If you rely on AI to generate your postings, you likely see a high volume of irrelevant applications.
tldr: AI drafts are generic and often contain hidden biases.
Treat AI output as a first draft, not a final document.
Always add specific team context, reporting lines, and the actual problem the role solves.
Use bias detection tools before publishing any job post.
Keep a human-approved record of every job description for legal compliance.

blocks.text: Why AI written job descriptions often fail

AI models are trained on existing job ads from across the internet. They tend to regress toward the mean. This means your job description ends up sounding exactly like every other company in your industry. When everything sounds the same, candidates cannot distinguish your company culture or the specific challenges of the role.
The hidden costs of automated drafting

The cost of using unedited AI text is not just time. It is the quality of your pipeline. When a job description is vague, you invite unqualified applicants to apply. You then spend hours screening resumes that do not match the actual requirements of the role. For regulated roles in healthcare or law, using generic AI text can also lead to compliance issues if the generated text includes requirements that violate local labor laws or company policies.
How to improve your recruitment workflow

items: Start with a raw AI draft to save time on formatting.
Use ⌘ + F in your browser to check for overused corporate buzzwords.
Add a section detailing the specific project the new hire will own in their first 90 days.
Review the draft against your internal diversity and inclusion guidelines.
Save a final version in a shared folder for future reference.

blocks.text: If you are hiring for regulated roles like nursing, law, or accounting, never include AI-generated requirements without verifying them against your employer's legal guidelines. AI may suggest certifications or tasks that do not align with your specific regional regulations or patient/client data privacy rules.
blocks.title: A note on regulated industries

faq.question: Should I stop using AI for job descriptions?
faq.answer: No, AI is a great tool for drafting. Just ensure you perform a human review to add company-specific details and remove generic filler.

faq.question: How do I make my job descriptions stand out?
faq.answer: Focus on the specific problem the role solves rather than just listing responsibilities. Candidates want to know the impact they will have.

causes.title: Lack of human oversight
causes.text: Recruiters often post AI drafts without adding the necessary company and role-specific context.

fixes.title: The 10-minute audit
fixes.text: Spend ten minutes adding details like reporting lines and team size to any AI-generated draft.

fixes.title: Bias check
fixes.text: Use a simple checklist to ensure your language is inclusive and free of exclusionary requirements.
